 Korean Brands Now Account for a Quarter of Skin Care VIT
 Data from Traackr shows that in the U.S., nearly one-fourth of online skin care buzz during the third quarter was driven by and about K-beauty brands.

 K-beauty’s slice of social media skin care buzz continues to soar. 
 Data from Traackr shows that during the third quarter, Korean brands drove nearly one-fourth of total skin care VIT in the U.S., which is Traackr’s brand vitality score metric assessing brands’ social media engagement and reach.
 Leading the charge was Medicube , which came in at a VIT score of 188,418 and thus held 6.9 percent share of total skin care VIT during the period. The brand also had 103,000 social media posts, making it the top brand by post count, as well.

 “Medicube is a great example of what sustained creator activity can do for a brand,” said Traackr chief executive officer Pierre-Loic Assayag, adding that the brand expanded its creator base by 35 percent quarter-over-quarter while simultaneously seeing sustained momentum with existing creators. “Nearly half of Medicube’s VIT this quarter came from creators who had also posted about it in the second quarter.” 
 Fellow K-beauty brand Anua , which added Kendall Jenner as its first celebrity ambassador in June, was the number-five brand by VIT with a score of 85,757, while Laneige came in at number 10. Assayag said that these brands also demonstrate standout creator retention, which in skin care is “one of the strongest signals of success.”
 L’Oréal’s dermatological brands, CeraVe and La Roche-Posay, were top-five players during the third quarter, comprising 6.5 percent and 4.7 percent share of skin care voice, respectively, while L’Oréal Paris — which ranks as the number-one brand when looking at cross-category VIT — was number eight in skin. 
 Two indies also broke through — Eadem, a 2021 graduate of Sephora’s Accelerate program known for its $24 Le Chouchou lip balm, and teen influencer Salish Matter’s Sincerely Yours , which debuted last year at Sephora and most recently added lip balms to its Gen Alpha-friendly range.
